ABOUT THE REPORT
[Content]
The Report is the tenth Environmental, Social and Governance ( 'ESG' ) Report of China Medical System Holdings Limited (the 'Company' , together with its subsidiaries, the 'Group' or 'CMS' ). This is an annual report, which covers the fiscal year from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025 (the 'Reporting Period' ) with some additional related information incorporated that may have occurred outside the Reporting Period.

text: The Report is prepared as per Appendix C2 Environmental, Social and Governance Reporting Code of Main Board Listing Rules issued by the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited ( 'HKEX' ), with reference to the SGX Core ESG Metrics published by the Singapore Exchange ( 'SGX' ). Meanwhile, the Report refers to and responds to issues concerned by the United Nations 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), MSCI-ESG rating, and S&P Corporate Sustainability Assessment (CSA), with the combination of the Company' s business development and ESG practices.

text: The Group focuses on unmet clinical needs and drives innovation through a dual approach of 'collaborative R&D and inhouse R&D' . text: The Company has formed a three-tier ESG governance framework consisting of the Board of Directors, the ESG Committee and the ESG Working Group. text: To further integrate ESG governance with the incentive system, the Group has formally established the CMS Non-financial Key Performance Indicators and Management Remuneration Linkage Mechanism . The mechanism incorporates key ESG indicators such as business ethics, product quality and safety, and climate change into the performance evaluation system for executive directors, senior management, and relevant management personnel, explicitly linking ESG indicators to 10% of the yearend bonus. This initiative aims to extend ESG targets from the strategic level of the Board of Directors to the front line of business implementation, promoting the management to comprehensively fulfill sustainability responsibilities while pursuing business performance. By directly linking ESG performance to remuneration incentives, the Group not only strengthens the execution of ESG initiatives, but also helps achieve an organic balance between long-term sustainable value and short-term operational performance, providing an institutional safeguard for its high-quality and responsible development.

text: The identification of material issues is a crucial step in building a sustainable development management system for enterprises. It helps clarify critical areas of responsibility and promotes the deep integration of ESG practices with strategic development. During the Reporting Period, the Group systematically reviewed sustainability-related issues by considering industry attributes, business characteristics, and changes in internal and external environments, and conducted the materiality assessment from two dimensions: 'impact on CMS' s finance and operations' (financial materiality) and 'impact on the economy, society, and environment' (impact materiality).

The identification of material issues is a crucial step in building a sustainable development management system for enterprises. It helps clarify critical areas of responsibility and promotes the deep integration of ESG practices with strategic development. During the Reporting Period, the Group systematically reviewed sustainability-related issues by considering industry attributes, business characteristics, and changes in internal and external environments, and conducted the materiality assessment from two dimensions: 'impact on CMS' s finance and operations' (financial materiality) and 'impact on the economy, society, and environment' (impact materiality).

The double materiality assessment this year was conducted through multiple approaches, including questionnaire and expert evaluations. During the Reporting Period, the Group engaged with stakeholders such as internal management, customers, suppliers, government authorities, and industry associations to thoroughly gather evaluations on the materiality of various ESG issues from both internal and external perspectives. A comprehensive analysis was conducted incorporating opinions from internal and external ESG experts.

text: Impact materiality assessment: Comprehensively considering both positive and negative impacts, actual and potential impacts, the Group assessed whether its performance on ESG-related issues would have significant impacts on the environment, economy, and society from dimensions such as impact scale, impact scope, probability of occurrence, and irreparability.

text:

Employees are required to strictly access, query and maintain personal and customer data with authorization, and unauthorized employees are not permitted to use, export or copy any customer information.
Access Inspection | The Group regularly inspects the information system access, including but not limited to the authorization mechanism, process, user access, access scope confirmation for in- service employees, and access clearance for departing employees. During the Reporting Period, the Group conducted an annual information system access inspection for internal office system cloud platform to ensure the reasonableness of access settings and security of the relevant data.
Confidentiality Management | The Group signs confidentiality agreements with employees, conveying and emphasizing the importance of confidentiality responsibilities and the legal consequences of breach. Employees are encouraged to prevent, stop, and report all related violations through channels such as telephone, email, and internal work software. For confidential data or personal information, sensitive information is desensitized.
External Collaboration | For suppliers who may have access to private information of consumers, the Group strictly constrains supplier behavior through contractual agreements, to protect customers' rights related to privacy and personal information.

text: The Group regards product quality and safety as the foundation of corporate sustainable development and has established a quality management system covering the entire value chain. Through an annual system review and dynamic revision mechanism, the Group ensures that the management system consistently complies with the latest regulations and industry requirements. It has formulated the CMS Management Provisions on the Direct Reporting of Quality Information to clarify the responsibilities of each business unit and the information reporting procedures, thus forming an efficient and transparent quality risk prevention and communication channel. In terms of product sourcing and standards control, the drug products promoted and sold by the Group are mainly produced by original manufacturers (suppliers) located in China, Germany, Denmark, the United Kingdom and France, in which the manufacturers are in strict compliance with the production quality management regulations of the countries where the drugs are produced. A small portion of the products are self-produced (during the Reporting Period, the sales contribution from self-produced products accounted for only approximately 0.7 % of the Group' s turnover in the case that all medicines were directly sold by the Group). All drugs promoted and sold by the Group have been registered and approved by relevant drug administration authorities (e.g., China NMPA). During the product manufacturing process, the Group performs regular calibration and maintenance of production equipment, and assigns dedicated personnel to monitor and record key process parameters throughout the entire process. The Group thoroughly inspects each batch of products to ensure the products are qualified and well-packed before entering the market. For specific products, samples are taken in strict accordance with national standards to test stability before delivery, to ensure that product quality aligns with national pharmaceutical standards. During the quality admission and acceptance process, the Group strictly inspects finished products in accordance with national product standards or product quality standards approved by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). For imported drug products, the Group strictly follows the requirements of national laws and regulations and undergoes stringent inspections by the Institute for Food and Drug Control, including the first batch of imported drugs, biological products, products after standard change or manufacturing process alteration, etc., and may require issuing the Import Inspection Report as necessary. Upon the arrival of the imported and domestic drug products, the Quality Management Department of the corresponding subsidiaries in drug operation business of the Group will conduct batch-by-batch inspections as per GSP requirements, and verify the product inspection reports. In case of any product quality issues, the Group will handle the problematic products by isolating, reporting, returning, or destroying them in accordance with the Operating Procedures for Reporting and Confirming Unqualified Drugs and the Operating Procedures for Destruction of Unqualified Drugs , ensuring that unqualified products never enter the market. In addition, the Group has established an independent special drug safety management system to implement stricter compliance management controls for specific products. For drugs under special control, the Group implements stricter control measures. The Group has formulated regulations on safety management of Diazepam Nasal Spray, which is a psychotropic drug of category II and was approved for marketing in 2023, and has set up separate warehouses for special drugs, with monitoring equipment installed and alarm devices connected to the public security system, in order to enhance the quality and safety management of drugs. For products that require refrigeration, the Group has set up independent refrigeration warehouses managed by designated personnel, equipped with essential hardware facilities, a round-the-clock automatic temperature and humidity monitoring system, etc., as well as emergency generators and emergency management plans to safeguard the quality and safety of drugs.

text: The Group implements hierarchical management for qualified suppliers according to the impact of their materials on product quality and safety. According to the Provisions for Material Supplier Management and the relationship between materials and key product quality, suppliers are classified into Grade I (primary/non-primary) suppliers and Grade II suppliers. Among them, Grade I suppliers provide materials that directly affect the key quality of products (such as raw and auxiliary materials, and packaging materials in direct contact with products), while Grade II suppliers provide materials that indirectly affect quality (such as external packaging materials, and testing reagents). The Quality Management Department of the Group conducts annual quality assessment on key material suppliers regularly, utilizing a comprehensive approach that includes qualification audits, sample testing, on-site audits, and document audits to perform multidimensional evaluations. Special emphasis is placed on conducting on-site quality audits for suppliers of primary raw and auxiliary materials, as well as internal packaging materials. During the Reporting Period, the Group completed on-site audits for 23 material suppliers. The Group has newly introduced the Regulations on Hierarchical Supplier Management . For new suppliers and stable suppliers, the Group conducts important scoring and hierarchical management according to quantitative indicators such as the annual procurement amount, the proportion of procurement amount to suppliers' revenue as well as suppliers' performance levels. Suppliers are categorized into four types: partner suppliers, key commercial suppliers, prior suppliers and commercial suppliers, achieving differentiated management of suppliers. text:
Supplier Selection | • Adhering to the principle of openness,fairness and impartiality, preventing and controlling possible corruption risks in the bidding process with participation of multiple departments; • Including human rights, environmental and social factors into the annual supplier assessment and review; encouraging and inclined to choose suppliers advocating the green environmental protection concept or with relevant qualifications, including but not limited to: ISO 14000, ISO 45001, SA8000, AEO, Transported Asset Protection Association (TAPA), etc.; • Under similar objective conditions, prioritizing the supplier that is geographically closer and more easily accessible if the candidates are on a par, in order to reduce the potential environmental pollution during transportation.
Procurement and Production | • Clearly stating quality integrity, supply integrity, anti-corruption and other compliance requirements in agreements signed with suppliers, and requiring suppliers to comply with national and industry standards related to product operations and production; • Formulating the Provisions for Material Supplier Management , which clearly defines the scope of supplier audits, including dimensions such as legal operation, product quality, environment and governance; • Requiring suppliers to comply with environmental standards for packaging materials. The inner packaging in contact with drugs is required to be at least the food-grade packaging to realize green packaging.
Logistics Transportation | • Conducting all-round assessment in terms of qualification and capacities, to ensure product quality during the distribution process and to minimize the potential impact of goods circulation on the surrounding environment; • Including environmental and social factors in selection criteria for logistics service providers and distributors, including enterprise qualification, warehousing and distribution capacities, staffing, operational management, channel coverage, response efficiency, reputation in the industry and dedication to environmental protection; • Prioritizing distributors with TAPA certification, complying with GSP requirements, larger scale in the sales region, comprehensive distribution channels coverage and dedication to social responsibility and environmental protection; • Adding relevant terms related to anti-corruption, anti-bribery and compliance operation to the cooperation contracts signed with logistics service providers and distributors, requiring logistics service providers and distributors to confirm their compliance with the Group's relevant provisions; • Conducting audits related to the Good Distribution Practice (GDP) for logistics service providers and regularly assessing and improving their operational quality; • Monitoring logistics service providers' environmental management practices and carbon emissions during the logistics processes, and sharing current measures available to control the increase in carbon emissions; • Providing training to international logistics service providers on related topics such as product transportation quality and environmental protection.

text: To systematically control and optimize corporate environmental practices, the Group has established an environmental governance system encompassing the Board of Directors, the ESG Committee under the Board, and the ESG Working Group. The Board of Directors of the Company is the highest-level governance body for environmental management strategy and performance. The ESG Committee under the Board is responsible for overseeing the management guidelines, policies and structures of environmental protection, overall supervising and managing ESG-related risks and opportunities, and collaborating with the Audit Department and the ESG Working Group to identify and address these risks. The ESG Working Group is primarily responsible for implementation, including the formulation of specific environmental management plans, the collection, consolidation, and analysis of data on pollution emissions, energy use, and water consumption from all responsible entities. These activities support reporting to the ESG Committee and assist the Board in continuously monitoring the Group' s management of energy conservation and emission reduction, as well as the achievement of environmental targets. During the Reporting Period, the Board of Directors of the Company and the ESG Committee reviewed the Group' s environmental management strategy, the implementation of environmental management, and the progress of environmental targets.

Hazardous and Non-hazardous Waste-Related Metrics and Targets The Group' s hazardous waste is mainly from laboratory waste liquids, expired chemical reagents and waste medicines, etc., in the pharmaceutical production and operation processes. text:

Classified Storage | √ Setting up a dedicated temporary hazardous waste storage room and warning signs, and storing hazardous waste in separate categories.
Compliant Handling | √ Engaging a third-party professional disposal company to transfer and dispose of hazardous waste on a regular basis. Before entering into hazardous waste disposal contracts with third parties, the Group strictly reviews their qualifications, such as the business license, the permits for operation and transportation.

ESG Aspects, General Disclosure and KPIs | Chapter
Part B: Mandatory Disclosure Requirements This part sets out disclosure requirements that must be included in an issuer' s ESG report on a mandatory basis.
Governance Structure | A statement from the board containing the following elements: (i) a disclosure of the board's oversight of ESG issues; (ii) the board's ESG management approach and strategy, including the process used to evaluate, prioritise and manage material ESG-related issues (including risks to the issuer's businesses); and (iii) how the board reviews progress made against ESG-related goals and targets with an explanation of how they relate to the issuer's businesses. | ESG Governance Strategy
Reporting Principles | Materiality: The ESG report should disclose: (i) the process to identify and the criteria for the selection of material ESG factors; (ii) if a stakeholder engagement is conducted, a description of significant stakeholders identified, and the process and results of the issuer's stakeholder engagement. | About the Report
A description of, or an explanation on, the application of the following Reporting Principles in the preparation of the ESG report: Quantitative: Information on the standards, methodologies, assumptions and/or calculation tools used, and source of conversion factors used, for the reporting of emissions/energy consumption (where applicable) should be disclosed. | About the Report
Consistency: The issuer should disclose in the ESG report any changes to the methods or KPIs used, or any other relevant factors affecting a meaningful comparison. | About the Report
Reporting Boundary | A narrative explaining the reporting boundaries of the ESG report and describing the process used to identify which entities or operations are included in the ESG report. If there is a change in the scope, the issuer should explain the difference and reason for the change. | About the Report
Part C: 'Comply or explain' Provisions This part sets out provisions to be reported on by an issuer in the ESG report on a 'comply or explain' basis.

text: 17 The indirect GHG emissions (Scope 2) mainly arise from indirect emissions due to the consumption of externally purchased electricity during the Group's operations and production processes. In 2025, 2024 and 2023, GHG emissions in Hong Kong were calculated with reference to the emission factors disclosed in HK Electric's Sustainability Report for 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively. For Macau, the emission factors applied in 2023 and 2024 were the operating-region emission factors; in 2025, GHG emissions in Macau were calculated with reference to the emission factors disclosed in Companhia de Electricidade de Macau (CEM)'s 2024 Sustainability Report. For operating locations outside Hong Kong and Macau, the relevant emission factors of the countries/regions were used. In particular, for 2025, the electricity emission factor for Mainland China adopted the grid emission factor of 0.5306 tCO2/MWh as specified in the Announcement on the release of the 2023 Electricity Carbon Dioxide Emission Factors, issued by the the Ministry of Ecology and Environment on 31 December 2025.
